//: Medarx — Orthanc configuration. WIRED IN PHASE 2, AS A DISPLAY SOURCE ONLY.
PHASE 2 DECISION (2026-09-28): `RemoteAccessAllowed` stays `false`, and the
browser reaches the archive through a loopback forwarder inside the
container instead. See `Dockerfile.orthanc` for the reasoning and
`compose.yaml` for the published-port mapping. Short version: turning the key
on in 1.10.1 automatically enables HTTP authentication, so the archive would
end up behind a credential that has to live in a tracked file or in the
image. Do not change it to make something work.
This is a DISPLAY integration. Orthanc serves image metadata and image data
to the OHIF viewport. No Medarx component reads pixels, and nothing in the
Medarx request path talks to this archive at all.
It is started by name:
and `docker compose -f infra/compose.yaml up -d` does not start this
container: the `orthanc` service is behind `profiles: ["orthanc"]` and
stays down until someone asks for it by name. It exists so that Phase 2
wires up a configuration that has been read rather than one assembled from
memory, and so the three DICOMweb gotchas below are written down next to
the file they will cost somebody an afternoon to rediscover.
GET /plugins  is the cheapest way to confirm the DICOMweb plugin loaded.
If /dicom-web is a 404 there, the image is jodogne/orthanc and not this one.
Name: Medarx-Phase1-Orthanc
// RemoteAccessAllowed: Orthanc ignores a key it does not know, silently. With the wrong key the
server starts, reports itself healthy, and answers every remote request with
401 - which reads exactly like an authentication problem and sends you to
look at credentials that were never the issue. This one cost a real
debugging session and it is the single most likely mistake anyone will make
Measured 2026-09-28 on this host, with the published port mapped straight
all answered 401, and the startup log said, in as many words,
`HTTP server listening on port: 8042 (HTTPS encryption is disabled,
remote access is not allowed)`. That is this key doing exactly what it says.
It stays false. The forwarder is the Phase 2 answer to the question this
// Authentication: Decision (Phase 2, 2026-10-31): no `Authentication` block, and none is added.
`RemoteAccessAllowed` stays `false`, so Orthanc enables no HTTP authentication.
The browser reaches the archive through the loopback forwarder in `entrypoint.sh`,
which Orthanc sees as local. Verified 2026-10-31: with the forwarder running,
`GET /dicom-web/studies` from the host returns 200. No credential exists to leak.
If one is ever needed it is set from the environment, never in this file.
// Plugins: THE KEY THAT MAKES DICOMWEB EXIST. Without this array Orthanc loads NO
plugins at all - not the DICOMweb one, not ServeFolders, nothing - and
GET /dicom-web/studies answers 404 while the server reports itself
healthy. Installing the orthanc-dicomweb package is necessary and not
sufficient; the plugin has to be pointed at.
The directory, not the library: Debian ships the versioned library
trixie) and the unversioned name as a symlink beside it. Naming the
directory is what survives a version bump.
Measured 2026-09-28 on this host, before and after: with the array absent,
`GET /dicom-web/studies` was 404 and the startup log said nothing about
plugins at all; with it present, the same log says
`Registering plugin 'dicom-web' (version 1.7)` and the same request is 200.
`GET /plugins` is NOT a sufficient check on its own. Measured 2026-10-31 on
this image it returned `[explorer.js, dicom-web, serve-folders, worklists]`,
so it can show the plugin, but it lists every registered plugin and an earlier
reading recorded only `[explorer.js]`. The check that cannot be fooled is the

// Logging: SystemFile and its level are left at Orthanc's defaults. A DICOM server's
log can name studies, series and SOP instance UIDs, and each one is an
identifier. Observed 2026-10-31: at the default level, the container log for
one STOW-RS of a synthetic study and the reads of its metadata contained no
UID. That is one run, not a policy. Named gap: the Orthanc log is not a Python
logger, so `medarx.logging_filter` does not cover it, and no sensitive-data
policy for DICOM traffic has been written. Writing one here would be inventing it.
